definition_zh: 问卷；问题表；调查表
definition_en: a written list of questions used to collect information from many people
core_image: 一叠印满问题的纸，被一张张分到路人手里填写
scene: 学会的志愿者站在街角，把一叠问题表一张张递到过路人手里。A volunteer handed each shopper a short questionary about local bus services.
sceneCN: 这里 questionary 是「问卷；问题表」（第 1 个义项：分发给许多人填写的成套问题）；句意：一名志愿者把一份关于当地公交服务的简短问卷递给了每位顾客。

derivatives.zh: 问题；提问
问卷；调查表（更常见的写法）
提问者；发问的人
带着疑问地；疑惑地

senses.title: A printed list of questions for many people
senses.definition: a set of written questions sent or handed to many people so that their answers can be collected
senses.definitionCN: 一份印好、分发给许多人作答并回收答案的成套问题
senses.example: The market researcher handed out a two-page questionary at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 市场调研员在车站发放了一份两页的问卷。
senses.why: The Latin root quaerere asks, so the noun first names a thing built for asking people questions.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 quaerere 意为「询问」，所以这个词首先指一件专门用来向人发问的东西。

senses.title: The instrument of a survey
senses.definition: the form used as the main tool of an inquiry, such as a survey or a census
senses.definitionCN: 作为调查、普查等征询活动主要工具的表格
senses.example: Each household received a census questionary by post.
senses.exampleCN: 每户人家都通过邮寄收到了一份人口普查表。
senses.why: Once it is used by an institution to gather data, the question form becomes a recognised instrument of inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 当它被机构用来收集数据时，这张问题表就成了调查工具，于是有了更正式的用法。

senses.title: An old spelling of questionnaire
senses.definition: a spelling of questionnaire that appears in older dictionaries and official texts
senses.definitionCN: 旧词典和较早的官方文件中出现的 questionnaire 拼写变体
senses.example: The museum archive keeps an old questionary from the first health check.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆档案里保存着第一轮健康普查时的一份旧问卷。
senses.why: The word entered English with the -ary ending of Latin, and the modern -aire spelling won only later.
senses.whyCN: 这个词借入英语时带着拉丁语的 -ary 词尾，现代通行的 -aire 拼写是后来才定下来的。

senses.title: A place where people ask and debate
senses.definition: an archaic use naming a place or body where questions are asked and argued
senses.definitionCN: 较古旧的用法，指人们提问、争论的场所或机构
senses.example: In late Victorian usage a questionary could mean a debating chamber.
senses.exampleCN: 在维多利亚时代晚期，这个词可以指辩论厅。
senses.why: Because the root means both to ask and to argue, rare older texts stretch the noun from a paper form to a place of questioning.
senses.whyCN: 词根同时有「询问」与「争辩」的含义，所以很罕见的旧文本把这个名词从纸面扩到发问的场所。

intro.en: Questionary comes from Latin quaerere, to ask, through the Latin adjective quaestionarius, a set of questions.
intro.cn: questionary 来自拉丁语 quaerere（询问），经由拉丁语形容词 quaestionarius（问题集）进入英语。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问、探究。

items.en: Quaestio and quaestionarius name a question or a set of questions.
items.cn: quaestio 与 quaestionarius 表示问题或成套问题。

items.en: Question and questioner pass through French into English.
items.cn: question 与 questioner 经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Questionary appears as a learned borrowing for a written list of questions.
items.cn: questionary 作为书面借词出现，指成书面的问题清单。

items.en: Questionnaire becomes the usual spelling, and questionary survives as an older variant.
items.cn: questionnaire 成为通行拼写，questionary 作为较早的变体保留下来。

note.en: Questionary sits inside the asking family of question, questionnaire, and query, and close to survey words.
note.cn: questionary 属于「询问」这一词族，与 question、questionnaire、query 同源，并与调查类词相邻。

entries.definition: a sentence that asks for an answer
entries.definitionCN: 提出问题、要求回答的句子

entries.definition: a written list of questions, the usual modern form
entries.definitionCN: 书面问题清单，现代通行写法

entries.definition: a question, often about something doubtful
entries.definitionCN: 疑问；询问，多指对某事存疑

entries.definition: a study that collects opinions or facts from many people
entries.definitionCN: 向许多人收集意见或事实的研究活动

entries.definition: a printed sheet with spaces to be filled in
entries.definitionCN: 印有空格待填写的表格

entries.definition: a count of opinions, especially political ones
entries.definitionCN: 民意调查，尤指政治调查

normalIntro.en: Questionary is a question sheet: the root asks, and the ending means a thing used for that purpose.
normalIntro.cn: questionary 就是「问题表」：词根表示发问，词尾表示用来做这件事的物件。

normal.en: The root quaerere means to ask, so a questionary is a set of asking.
normal.cn: 词根 quaerere 表示询问，所以 questionary 就是一整套提问。

normal.en: The -ary ending often marks a thing used for a purpose, as in library or dictionary.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ary 常标记「用于某用途的物品」，如 library 与 dictionary。

normal.en: Questionary and questionnaire are the same word with two endings, and questionnaire is now more common.
normal.cn: questionary 与 questionnaire 是同一词的两个词尾，如今 questionnaire 更常见。

normal.en: The plural is questionaries, with the y changing to ie before s.
normal.cn: 复数写作 questionaries，词尾 y 在 s 前变为 ie。

normal.en: Compare question: a question is one item, while a questionary is the whole sheet.
normal.cn: 对比 question：question 是一个问题，questionary 是整张问题表。

abstract.en: Picture a thick stack of papers covered in question marks.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠厚厚的纸，上面全是问号。

abstract.en: Imagine a clipboard that carries the whole census through a village.
abstract.cn: 想象一块写字板带着整份普查表走过一个村庄。

abstract.en: Think of an old book page where the ending -aire has not yet replaced -ary.
abstract.cn: 想象一页旧书，那时词尾 -aire 还没有取代 -ary。

examples.en: Please complete the questionary and return it to the front desk.
examples.cn: 请填好问卷后交回前台。

examples.en: Only half of the questionaries were returned to the research team.
examples.cn: 只有一半的问卷被交回给了研究团队。

examples.en: The lecturer cited a nineteenth-century questionary on school hygiene.
examples.cn: 讲师引用了一份十九世纪关于学校卫生的问卷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「快死瞧那里」——路上有人拦住你「快」问，让你「瞧」那张表填；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 quaerere（寻求、询问）→ quaestio（问题）→ quaestionarius（问题集）→ 英语 questionary，核心义「用来向人发问的一整套问题」。

sensesIntro.en: Questionary starts as a written list of questions for many people, then names the tool of a survey, then survives as an older spelling of questionnaire, and rarely as a place of debate.
sensesIntro.cn: questionary 先指发给许多人填写的问题表，再指调查所用工具，后来作为 questionnaire 的较早拼写保留，极少见时还指发问辩论的场所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of question sheets handed from person to person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠问题纸在人与人之间传递。

branches.en: The everyday sense is the sheet of questions for many people.
branches.cn: 日常义项是发给许多人填写的问题纸。

branches.en: The survey sense treats the sheet as a data tool.
branches.cn: 调查义项把这张纸当作收集数据的工具。

branches.en: The spelling sense keeps the old -ary ending alive in print.
branches.cn: 拼写义项让旧的 -ary 词尾在书面上继续存活。

branches.en: The archaic sense stretches asking into a place of debate.
branches.cn: 古旧义项把「发问」延伸到辩论场所。

branches.en: The sheet and the survey are two sides of the same asking.
branches.cn: 问题表与调查是同一「发问」行为的两面。

intro.en: Questionary is built from the Latin asking root quaerere plus the -ary ending that marks a thing or place.
intro.cn: questionary 由拉丁语表「询问」的词根 quaerere 加词尾 -ary 构成，-ary 常表示某类物品或场所。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere means to seek or ask, and its family gives question, quest, inquire, and questionary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quaerere 意为寻求、询问，其词族衍生出 question、quest、inquire 与 questionary。

items.example: Quaerere gives the asking image.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 提供「询问」的意象。

items.example: Quaestio is the noun of asking.
items.exampleCN: quaestio 是表示「发问」的名词。

items.example: Question drops into everyday speech.
items.exampleCN: question 进入日常用语。

items.meaning: a thing or place connected with
items.meaningCN: 与……有关的物品或场所的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ary forms questionary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成 questionary。

items.example: Questionary names the printed sheet.
items.exampleCN: questionary 指印好的问题表。

items.example: The ending -aire replaces -ary in questionnaire.
items.exampleCN: questionnaire 用 -aire 取代了 -ary。

items.meaning: the usual modern word for a question sheet
items.example: Questionnaire is now the more common form.
items.exampleCN: questionnaire 如今是更常见的词形。

items.example: The suffix -er forms questioner.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 questioner。

items.example: Questioner names the person asking.
items.exampleCN: questioner 指提问的人。

definition_zh: 安静；寂静；平静；文静
definition_en: the state or quality of being quiet, with little or no noise, activity, or disturbance
core_image: 雪后的村子，屋门紧闭，连狗都不叫一声
scene: 深夜的图书馆里，翻页声都显得很大，所有人都压低声音。The quietness of the room made every footstep sound loud.
sceneCN: 这里 quietness 是「安静；寂静」（第 1 个义项：没有声音的状态）；句意：房间的安静让每一次脚步声都显得很响。

derivatives.zh: 安静的；安静
安静地；轻声地
（英）使安静；安静下来
不安的；不平静的

senses.title: The condition of little or no noise
senses.definition: the condition of having or making very little sound
senses.definitionCN: 声音极少或完全没有声音的状态
senses.example: The quietness of the library helped her finish the essay.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆的安静帮她写完了论文。
senses.why: Latin quies means rest and stillness, and the noun first names the soundless state itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quies 意为休息与静止，所以这个词首先指「没有声音」的状态本身。

senses.title: Calm without movement or disturbance
senses.definition: a peaceful state without hurry, trouble, or disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 没有匆忙、纷扰或打扰的平和状态
senses.example: They escaped to the village for the quietness of country life.
senses.exampleCN: 他们躲到村子里，享受乡村生活的宁静。
senses.why: Stillness of sound extends easily to stillness of life, so quietness also names a calm and settled state.
senses.whyCN: 声音的静止很容易延伸为生活的静止，因此安静也指平和安稳的状态。

senses.title: A reserved, unshowy manner
senses.definition: a personal manner that is restrained, calm, and not showy
senses.definitionCN: 克制、沉稳、不张扬的处事作风
senses.example: Her quietness at meetings hid a very sharp mind.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上话不多，却掩藏着非常敏锐的头脑。
senses.why: Someone who stays still also keeps opinions to themselves, so a silent habit becomes a character quality.
senses.whyCN: 静坐不动的人也常把意见收在心里，于是「少言」从习惯变成了性格品质。

senses.title: A period when things are calm
senses.definition: a period of calm in business, politics, or public events
senses.definitionCN: 商务、政治或公共活动中平静无事的一段时期
senses.example: After the election the press enjoyed a short quietness.
senses.exampleCN: 选举过后，新闻界享受了短暂的平静。
senses.why: A long stretch of no news or no conflict is stillness spread out in time, so the state becomes a named period.
senses.whyCN: 很长一段时间没有新闻或没有冲突，就是被拉长到时间轴上的「静止」，于是这种状态被指名成一段时期。

senses.title: A quiet part of a place
senses.definition: a quiet spot or part of a building, town, or landscape
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、城镇或景致中安静的角落、地段
senses.example: She found a quietness at the far end of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 她在花园尽头找到一处幽静的地方。
senses.why: The noun can stand in for the place that has the quality, a common shift from state to spot.
senses.whyCN: 名词常可代指具有该性质的地方，这是由状态转向地点的常见引申。

intro.en: Quietness comes from Latin quies, rest and stillness, through Latin quietus and Old French quiet, with the English suffix -ness added to quiet.
intro.cn: quietness 来自拉丁语 quies（休息、静止），经拉丁语 quietus 与古法语 quiet 进入英语，再加上英语词尾 -ness。

items.en: Quies means rest, repose, or freedom from trouble.
items.cn: quies 意为休息、安歇、免于纷扰。

items.en: Quietus means calm or at rest.
items.cn: quietus 意为平静的、安息的。

items.en: Quiet and quiete pass into Middle English.
items.cn: quiet 与 quiete 传入中古英语。

items.en: Quiet names a state of rest and freedom from noise.
items.cn: 中古英语 quiet 指休息、安静的状态。

items.en: The suffix -ness turns quiet into the abstract noun quietness.
items.cn: 词尾 -ness 把 quiet 变成抽象名词 quietness。

note.en: Quietness belongs with quiet and quietly, and sits close to silence, calm, and peace.
note.cn: quietness 与 quiet、quietly 同族，并与 silence、calm、peace 这些近义词相邻。

entries.definition: making little or no noise
entries.definitionCN: 安静的；不出声的

entries.definition: in a quiet way
entries.definitionCN: 安静地；轻声地

entries.definition: to make or become quiet
entries.definitionCN: 使安静；安静下来

entries.definition: complete absence of sound
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有声音

entries.definition: a peaceful state without worry or motion
entries.definitionCN: 无忧无扰、不动的平静

entries.definition: freedom from noise, war, or disturbance
entries.definitionCN: 无噪声、无战争、无纷扰的状态

normalIntro.en: Quietness is the noun of quiet: the Latin root rests, and -ness turns the quality into a state.
normalIntro.cn: quietness 是 quiet 的名词形式：拉丁词根表示「安息、静止」，-ness 把这种性质变成一种状态。

normal.en: The Latin root quies means rest, which is why quietness feels calm rather than empty.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 quies 表示休息，所以 quietness 给人安宁的感觉，而不只是空无一物。

normal.en: The suffix -ness builds nouns from adjectives, as in kindness and darkness.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ness 把形容词变成名词，如 kindness 与 darkness。

normal.en: Quiet means calm resting, in contrast with the busy verb to quit, which means to leave.
normal.cn: quiet 表示静静休息，与表示离开的动词 quit 意思完全不同。

normal.en: The related verb quieten is common in British English, while quiet down is more American.
normal.cn: 相关动词 quieten 在英式英语中常见，美式则多说 quiet down。

normal.en: Compare silence: silence can be total, but quietness usually keeps a little soft sound.
normal.cn: 对比 silence：silence 可以是完全的无声，而 quietness 往往还留着一点轻响。

abstract.en: Picture a snowy village where no dog barks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个雪后的村子，没有一条狗在叫。

abstract.en: Imagine a phone switched off for the whole evening.
abstract.cn: 想象一整晚关掉的手机。

abstract.en: Think of a guest who listens more than she speaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一位听得多、说得少的客人。

examples.en: Visitors often come to the island for its quietness.
examples.cn: 游客常为这座岛的宁静而来。

examples.en: A sudden quietness fell over the classroom when the head teacher entered.
examples.cn: 校长一进来，教室里便突然安静下来。

examples.en: He answered with a gentle quietness that surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 他平静温和地回答，让所有人都很意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「快挨特耐斯」——吵得快要挨到痛处，只有安静能对付；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 quies（休息、静止）→ quietus（平静的）→ 古法语 quiet → 英语 quiet（安静的）→ 加 -ness 构成抽象名词 quietness，核心义「静止无声的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Quietness moves from absence of noise to calm of life, to a reserved manner, to a calm period, and finally to a quiet spot.
sensesIntro.cn: quietness 从「没有声音」扩展到「生活安宁」、再指「为人文静」、「平静时期」，最后可指「安静的地方」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silent village after snow, doors shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：雪后的村庄，万籁俱寂，屋门紧闭。

branches.en: The sound sense is the basic everyday meaning.
branches.cn: 声音义项是最基本的日常含义。

branches.en: Calm of life grows out of stillness of sound.
branches.cn: 生活的安宁由声音的静止生长而来。

branches.en: A silent person turns the state into a character quality.
branches.cn: 沉默的人把这状态转化为性格品质。

branches.en: A calm period and a quiet spot name when and where the state happens.
branches.cn: 平静时期与幽静处分别指这种状态发生的时间与地点。

branches.en: Both no noise and calm life rest on the same Latin stillness.
branches.cn: 无声与安宁都建立在同一个拉丁语「静止」之上。

intro.en: Quietness is quiet plus the native suffix -ness, with the Latin rest root quies at its base.
intro.cn: quietness 由 quiet 加本族语词尾 -ness 构成，词基可追溯到拉丁语表示「休息」的 quies。

latinIntro.en: Latin quies means rest and stillness, giving quiet, quietude, and indirectly the English set quiet, quietly, and quietness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quies 意为休息与静止，衍生出 quiet、quietude，并进而产生英语的 quiet、quietly 与 quietness。

items.example: Quies gives the rest image.
items.exampleCN: quies 提供「休息」的意象。

items.example: Quietus passes on through French.
items.exampleCN: quietus 经法语传来。

items.example: Quiet is the everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: quiet 是日常形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms quietness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 quietness。

items.example: Quietness names the state.
items.exampleCN: quietness 表示这种状态。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms quietly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 quietly。

items.example: Quietly is the adverb of quiet.
items.exampleCN: quietly 是 quiet 的副词形式。

items.example: The suffix -en forms quieten.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 构成 quieten。

items.example: Quieten turns the adjective into a verb.
items.exampleCN: quieten 把这个形容词变成动词。

definition_zh: 颤抖；颤动；抖动；箭袋；箭筒
definition_en: to shake with a slight, rapid movement, or a container worn on the back for carrying arrows
core_image: 弓弦被拉满后仍在颤动，一旁背箭袋的射手屏住呼吸
scene: 寒风里，她拉满弓久久不放，指尖微微发抖，背上的箭袋轻轻晃动。Her hand began to quiver as she held the heavy bow.
sceneCN: 这里 quiver 是「颤抖；颤动」（第 1 个义项：身体部位因寒冷、紧张或用力而快速轻抖）；句意：她握着沉重弓时手开始颤抖。

collocations.phrase: slip an arrow from the quiver

derivatives.zh: 颤抖的；颤动的
颤抖地
一箭袋的量

senses.title: For a body part to shake slightly
senses.definition: for a hand, lip, or other body part to shake with a light, fast movement
senses.definitionCN: 手、嘴唇等身体部位以轻快小幅的动作抖动
senses.example: Her lips quivered when she read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她读那封信时嘴唇发抖。
senses.why: The Old English verb cwifer, meaning nimble or lively, gave a word for quick repeated motion, which names a body that cannot keep still.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cwifer 意为「敏捷、活泼」，先表示快速重复的动作，再用来形容无法保持不动的身体部位。

senses.title: To tremble with a strong feeling
senses.definition: to tremble because of fear, cold, anger, or excitement
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧、寒冷、愤怒或激动而颤抖
senses.example: He quivered with anger but said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他气得发抖，却什么也没说。
senses.why: Strong feeling sets the muscles in fast small tremors, so the physical shake stands for the emotion behind it.
senses.whyCN: 强烈情绪会让肌肉发生快速的小幅震颤，所以这个身体动作可以代表背后的情感。

senses.title: For a thing to vibrate
senses.definition: for a leaf, string, surface, or light to move with a fine rapid shaking
senses.definitionCN: 叶片、琴弦、表面或光影发生细密快速的抖动
senses.example: The leaves quivered in the morning wind.
senses.exampleCN: 叶子在晨风中颤动。
senses.why: The quick light movement is not limited to people, so the verb spreads to anything that shakes in a fine way.
senses.whyCN: 这种轻快的动作并不限于人，于是动词延伸到任何轻微振动的东西。

senses.title: A container for carrying arrows
senses.definition: a case worn on the back or at the belt for holding arrows
senses.definitionCN: 背在背上或系在腰间用来装箭的筒袋
senses.example: The archer pulled an arrow from his quiver.
senses.exampleCN: 弓箭手从箭袋里抽出一支箭。
senses.why: The noun for the arrow case comes from a different source, borrowed from Old French quivre, and only shares the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 表示箭袋的名词另有来源，借自古法语 quivre，只是与动词拼写相同。

senses.title: A shaking movement or sound
senses.definition: a slight rapid shaking, or a trembling sound such as a quivering voice
senses.definitionCN: 轻微快速的抖动，或发颤的声音（如颤抖的嗓音）
senses.example: There was a nervous quiver in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他的声音里带着紧张的颤抖。
senses.why: English turns many verbs into nouns of one instance, so a quiver is a single spell of the trembling action.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动词转成表示「一次动作」的名词，所以 a quiver 就是一次颤抖的动作。

intro.en: Quiver has two histories behind one spelling: the trembling verb is usually traced to an Old English adjective meaning nimble, while the arrow case comes from Old French.
intro.cn: quiver 同一个拼写背后有两段历史：表示颤抖的动词一般追溯到古英语中意为「敏捷」的形容词，而箭袋一词则来自古法语。

items.en: The adjective cwifer means nimble or lively, giving a sense of quick motion.
items.cn: 古英语形容词 cwifer 意为敏捷、活泼，带有快速运动的意味。

items.en: Quiver names a light rapid shaking of the body.
items.cn: 中古英语 quiver 指身体轻微快速的抖动。

items.en: The arrow case comes from Old French quivre or cuivre, of uncertain ultimate origin.
items.cn: 箭袋一词来自古法语 quivre 或 cuivre，其更早来源尚不确定。

items.en: Quiver also names the case in which an archer carries arrows.
items.cn: 中古英语 quiver 也指弓箭手装箭的袋筒。

items.en: Quiver keeps both the trembling verb and the arrow noun, and adds a noun for a shaking sound.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了颤抖动词与箭袋名词，并增添了表示颤动的名词用法。

note.en: Quiver is a light shaking word, close in form to words with -iver and in meaning to tremble and shiver.
note.cn: quiver 是表示「轻颤」的词，形式上与 -iver 类词相近，意义上与 tremble、shiver 相邻。

entries.definition: to shake, especially of the voice
entries.definitionCN: 颤抖，尤指声音发颤，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to shake because of cold or fear
entries.definitionCN: 因寒冷或恐惧而发抖，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a large natural stream of water
entries.definitionCN: 河流，只是押韵，词源不同

entries.definition: to shake with small quick movements
entries.definitionCN: 以细小的动作颤抖

entries.definition: to shake strongly, usually from fear or disgust
entries.definitionCN: 剧烈抖动，多因恐惧或厌恶

entries.definition: a small shaking movement
entries.definitionCN: 轻微的抖动；震颤

normalIntro.en: Quiver is a word of quick light motion: the trembling verb comes from an Old English word for nimble, and the arrow case comes from French.
normalIntro.cn: quiver 是表示「快速轻微动作」的词：颤抖义来自古英语「敏捷」，箭袋义则来自法语。

normal.en: Think of the Old English cwifer, meaning nimble, which lies behind the trembling quiver.
normal.cn: 记住古英语 cwifer 意为敏捷，它就是颤抖义 quiver 的来源。

normal.en: Quiver with fear or quiver with cold shows the feeling that sets the shaking.
normal.cn: quiver with fear 或 quiver with cold 点出引起发抖的情绪或环境。

normal.en: The plural and third person both use quivers, and the past tense doubles the r in quivered.
normal.cn: 复数与三单都写作 quivers，过去式则把 r 写成双写 quivered。

normal.en: Compare shiver: shiver is cold shaking, quiver is finer and can be one hand or one lip.
normal.cn: 对比 shiver：shiver 多指因寒冷而发抖，quiver 幅度更小，可以是手或嘴唇。

normal.en: Compare quaver: quaver is usually the voice, quiver can be the whole body or a leaf.
normal.cn: 对比 quaver：quaver 多用于声音，quiver 可指全身或叶片。

abstract.en: Picture a bowstring still humming after the shot.
abstract.cn: 想象一枝箭射出后，弓弦仍在嗡嗡颤动。

abstract.en: Imagine a cold hand holding a hot cup of tea.
abstract.cn: 想象一只冰冷的手端着一杯热茶。

abstract.en: Think of an archer reaching back for an arrow.
abstract.cn: 想象弓箭手反手去背后摸箭。

examples.en: His hands quivered slightly as he opened the envelope.
examples.cn: 他拆信封时双手微微发抖。

examples.en: The archer carried a leather quiver across his shoulder.
examples.cn: 弓箭手肩上挎着一个皮箭袋。

examples.en: The lake quivered for a moment after the stone fell.
examples.cn: 石头落入水中后，湖面颤动了一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「快微」——快而微微地抖；或者「盔窝」——放箭的筒窝在背上；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 颤抖义一般认为来自古英语 cwifer（敏捷、活泼），核心义「快速轻微的动作」；箭袋义借自古法语 quivre（更早来源不确定），两义同形不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Quiver begins with a body part shaking lightly, extends to trembling with feeling and to things vibrating, then adds a separate French-borrowed noun for the arrow case and a noun for one shake.
sensesIntro.cn: quiver 从身体部位的轻颤出发，扩展到因情绪而发抖和物体颤动，另有借自法语的箭袋名词，以及表示一次抖动的名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowstring still trembling after the arrow is loosed.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭已离弦，弓弦仍在颤动。

branches.en: A shaking body part is the basic physical sense.
branches.cn: 身体部位发抖是最基本的身体义项。

branches.en: Trembling with feeling adds the emotional layer.
branches.cn: 因情绪而发抖为它增添了情感层面。

branches.en: Things vibrate and produce a quiver of sound.
branches.cn: 物体颤动并产生发颤的声音。

branches.en: The arrow case is a separate borrowing that shares only the spelling.
branches.cn: 箭袋义是另一来源的借词，只与动词共享拼写。

branches.en: All three share the fine rapid shaking that the core image shows.
branches.cn: 前三个义项都共享核心意象中那种细密快速的抖动。

intro.en: Quiver is mostly a whole word rather than a prefixed form, built round an Old English base for nimble motion and a French noun for the arrow case.
intro.cn: quiver 基本是整体词而不是前缀派生词，围绕古英语表示敏捷动作的词基与法语箭袋名词构成。

latinIntro.en: The trembling verb has no Latin root; it is usually traced to Old English cwifer, meaning nimble, while the arrow case comes from Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 表示颤抖的动词没有拉丁词根，一般追溯到古英语 cwifer（敏捷），而箭袋名词来自古法语。

items.meaningCN: 敏捷的；活泼的（一般认为的古英语形式）
items.example: The Old English adjective gives quick motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语形容词提供「快速动作」的含义。

items.example: Quiver is the trembling verb.
items.exampleCN: quiver 是表示颤抖的动词。

items.meaning: to do something again and again
items.example: The suffix -er adds the idea of repeated shaking.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 加上反复颤动的意味。

items.example: The French noun gives the arrow case.
items.exampleCN: 法语名词提供箭袋义。

items.meaning: as many arrows as a quiver holds
items.example: The compound quiverful joins noun and -ful.
items.exampleCN: 合成词 quiverful 由名词加 -ful 构成。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms quivering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 quivering。

items.example: Quivering describes a shaking thing.
items.exampleCN: quivering 形容正在颤抖的事物。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms quiveringly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 quiveringly。

definition_zh: 提醒；提示；催单；使人想起某事的纪念物
definition_en: a person, thing, or message that makes you remember something you might forget
core_image: 一张贴在冰箱门上的便条，写着待办的事
scene: 冰箱门上贴着一张便条，提醒她明早去看牙医。A note on the fridge door serves as a reminder to visit the dentist in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 reminder 是「提醒物；提示」（第 1 个义项：帮助人记住某事的东西）；句意：冰箱门上的便条提醒她早上去看牙医。场景要点：便条、马克笔、冰箱贴。

collocations.zh: 对……的提醒；令人想起……的事物

derivatives.zh: 动词原形，义为「提醒；使想起」
旧用法形容词，义为「已被提醒的」（少用）
动名词转名词，义为「提醒的行为」

senses.title: Something that helps you remember
senses.definition: a message, note, or signal that makes you remember to do something
senses.definitionCN: 便条、信息或信号，让人记得去做某事
senses.example: He left a reminder on the table about the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他在桌上留了一张关于会议的提醒。
senses.why: The suffix -er turns remind into the thing that does the reminding, so the word names the note itself.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 把 remind 变成「起提醒作用的东西」，所以这个词直接指那张便条。

senses.title: A formal or official notice
senses.definition: an official letter or notice asking someone to pay or to do something by a deadline
senses.definitionCN: 要求某人付款或在期限内做某事的正式函件或通知
senses.example: The bank sent a final reminder about the unpaid loan.
senses.exampleCN: 银行寄来了一封关于未还贷款的最终催款通知。
senses.why: When a message is repeated on purpose and with authority, the reminder becomes a formal demand.
senses.whyCN: 当一条信息被有意地、带着权威地反复传达，提醒就升级为正式的催办要求。

senses.title: A person or event that brings back a memory
senses.definition: a person, sound, smell, or event that brings something back to mind
senses.definitionCN: 让人重新想起往事的人、声音、气味或事件
senses.example: That song is a reminder of my first summer at the seaside.
senses.exampleCN: 那首歌让我想起在海边度过的第一个夏天。
senses.why: The root mind carries memory as well as attention, so the word can also mean a trigger of memory.
senses.whyCN: 词根 mind 既含「注意」也含「记忆」，因此这个词还能表示勾起记忆的触发点。

senses.title: A warning example
senses.definition: an event or situation that shows you what could happen if you are not careful
senses.definitionCN: 显示若不小心会发生什么的事件或处境
senses.example: The accident was a reminder that safety rules matter.
senses.exampleCN: 这起事故提醒人们安全规则很重要。
senses.why: A reminder can point forward as well as backward, showing a future risk through a past event.
senses.whyCN: 提醒既可以回溯过去，也可以指向将来，借过去的事件预示未来的风险。

intro.en: Reminder is remind plus the agent suffix -er, and remind is re- plus the Old English verb myndan, to think of or pay attention to.
intro.cn: reminder 是 remind 加上施动后缀 -er；remind 由 re- 与古英语动词 myndan（想到、留心）构成。

items.en: The verb myndan means to remember or pay attention to something.
items.cn: 古英语动词 myndan 意为记得或留心某事。

items.en: The Latin root ment appears in English mind, meaning the thinking faculty.
items.cn: 拉丁词根 ment 出现在英语 mind 中，指思维能力。

items.en: The verb remind is formed again with Latin re- attached to mind.
items.cn: 动词 remind 以拉丁前缀 re- 加 mind 重新构成。

items.en: Reminder appears as remind plus the agent suffix -er.
items.cn: reminder 由 remind 加上施动后缀 -er 出现。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to digital alerts and payment notices.
items.cn: 现代英语把该词扩展到电子提醒与付款通知。

note.en: Reminder belongs to the remind family and sits close to memory words and to official notice words.
note.cn: reminder 属于「提醒」词族，既靠近记忆类词，也靠近正式通知类词。

entries.definition: to make someone remember something
entries.definitionCN: 提醒；使想起

entries.definition: the faculty of thought and memory
entries.definitionCN: 心智；头脑

entries.definition: the part that is left over
entries.definitionCN: 剩余部分；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a signal that tells someone to act
entries.definitionCN: 提示；提示符

entries.definition: an official announcement or warning
entries.definitionCN: 通知；告示

entries.definition: an object kept to remember a person or event
entries.definitionCN: 纪念品；纪念物

normalIntro.en: Reminder is literally the thing that re-minds you, pushing a fact back into your mind.
normalIntro.cn: reminder 字面就是「重新让你想到」的东西，把一个事实再推回你的头脑。

normal.en: The suffix -er marks the thing that does the reminding.
normal.cn: 后缀 -er 标示「起提醒作用的东西」。

normal.en: Set a reminder means using a phone or clock to tell you later.
normal.cn: set a reminder 就是用手机或闹钟稍后提醒你。

normal.en: A reminder of something points back to it, like a song or a photo.
normal.cn: a reminder of something 指向某个事物，比如一首歌或一张照片。

normal.en: Payment reminder is the polite way a company asks for money.
normal.cn: payment reminder 是公司礼貌地催款的称呼。

normal.en: Do not confuse reminder with remainder, which means what is left.
normal.cn: 不要把 reminder 与 remainder 混淆，后者意为剩下的部分。

abstract.en: Picture a sticky note curling on the fridge door.
abstract.cn: 想象一张便条贴在冰箱门上，边角微微卷起。

abstract.en: Imagine an envelope marked final and placed in a tray.
abstract.cn: 想象一只标着「最终」的信封被放进文件盘。

abstract.en: Hear a song from a sunny summer and see the sea again.
abstract.cn: 听见一首夏日之歌，眼前又浮现海面。

examples.en: Please send me a gentle reminder before the deadline.
examples.cn: 请在截止日期前给我一个善意的提醒。

examples.en: The old photo is a reminder of our school days.
examples.cn: 这张旧照片让我想起学生时代。

examples.en: The bank charged a fee after sending two reminders.
examples.cn: 银行在发出两次催单后收取了费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞迈恩的」——瑞气满满地迈步，靠一张便条提醒自己别忘事；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 myndan（想到、留心）+ 拉丁词根 ment（心智）→ mind；再以拉丁前缀 re-（再）加 mind 构成 remind，最后加施动后缀 -er 成 reminder，核心义「把某事再度放进心里」。

sensesIntro.en: Reminder starts as the note that re-minds you, extends to official notices, then to anything that brings back a memory, and finally to a warning example.
sensesIntro.cn: reminder 先指「让你重新想起的便条」，再扩展为正式通知，进而指勾起回忆的事物，最后指警示性的前车之鉴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sticky note on the fridge door.
core.cn: 核心意象：冰箱门上的一张便条。

branches.en: The everyday note is the concrete sense.
branches.cn: 日常便条是最具体的义项。

branches.en: A repeated message from an authority becomes a formal notice.
branches.cn: 权威方反复传达的信息变成正式通知。

branches.en: Anything that re-minds can also revive a memory.
branches.cn: 任何能「重新提醒」的东西也能唤起回忆。

branches.en: Both a note and a shocking event push a fact back into your mind.
branches.cn: 便条与震惊的事件都会把某个事实再推回你的脑中。

branches.en: Official notices and warning examples both urge timely action.
branches.cn: 正式通知与警示案例都催促人及时行动。

intro.en: Reminder is built from re-, the verb mind, and the agent suffix -er, the same pattern as user or builder.
intro.cn: reminder 由 re-、动词 mind 与施动后缀 -er 构成，和 user、builder 的构词方式一样。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -er comes from Latin -arius through Old French, meaning a person or thing that performs an action.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -er 经古法语来自拉丁语 -arius，表示执行动作的人或物。

items.example: The prefix re- gives the sense of bringing back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 带来「带回、再度」之意。

items.meaning: the memory and the act of attending
items.example: Mind carries both memory and attention.
items.exampleCN: mind 同时承载记忆与注意。

items.example: Remind is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: remind 是这个名词背后的动词。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er makes the note the doer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 让便条成为施动者。

items.example: A reminder stays concrete and countable.
items.exampleCN: reminder 具体且可数。

items.example: Phones store many reminders.
items.exampleCN: 手机里存着许多提醒。

items.example: Reminding takes patience and tact.
items.exampleCN: 提醒需要耐心与技巧。

items.example: Unmindful builds on the same mind root.
items.exampleCN: unmindful 共享同一个 mind 词根。

items.example: Mindful shows the adjective pattern of mind.
items.exampleCN: mindful 展示 mind 的形容词构词方式。

items.example: Memory belongs to the same remembering field.
items.exampleCN: memory 属于同一个记忆语义场。

latinEntries.meaning: one who or that which acts

definition_zh: 汇款；宽恕；职责范围；暂时缓解
definition_en: to send money to someone, or to forgive a debt and reduce a punishment
core_image: 一只信封从一只手递到远方，里面的欠条被划掉
scene: 公司每月向海外的供应商汇款一次。The company chooses to remit a payment to its overseas supplier each month.
sceneCN: 这里 remit 是「汇款」（第 1 个义项：把钱寄给某人）；句意：公司每个月都向海外供应商汇款一次。场景要点：信封、银行柜面、跨国汇单。

derivatives.zh: 由 remit 加 -ance 构成，义为「汇款；汇款额」
由 remit 加 -ssion 构成，义为「宽恕；病势缓解」
由 remit 加 -ent 构成，义为「间歇性的」

senses.title: To send money as payment
senses.definition: to send money to a person or place, especially as payment
senses.definitionCN: 把钱寄给某人或某地，尤指作为付款
senses.example: Migrant workers remit money to their families every month.
senses.exampleCN: 外来务工者每月给家里汇款。
senses.why: The prefix re- means back, and mittere means to send, so the money is literally sent back home.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示「回」，mittere 表示「送」，钱在字面上就是被寄回家乡。

senses.title: To forgive a debt or punishment
senses.definition: to officially forgive a debt, fine, or punishment and decide that it need not be paid or carried out
senses.definitionCN: 正式免除债款、罚款或刑罚，决定不必支付或执行
senses.example: The court remitted part of the fine after the appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉之后，法院免除了部分罚款。
senses.why: What is sent back can also be an obligation, so the word comes to mean letting a debt go.
senses.whyCN: 被「退回」的不仅是钱，也可以是一项义务，于是这个词引申为「让债务一笔勾销」。

senses.title: Leaving an illness or losing force
senses.definition: to become less severe or to stop, used of a fever, symptoms, or an effort
senses.definitionCN: 病情、症状或力量变得不那么严重或停止
senses.example: The fever usually remits within three days of treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗之后，发热通常在三天内缓解。
senses.why: Medical use treats symptoms as something that can be sent back and let go of.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把症状看作可以被「退回、放开」的东西，因此引申为缓解消退。

senses.title: To refer a matter to another body
senses.definition: to send a case or question to a higher court or an authority for a decision
senses.definitionCN: 把案件或问题送交上级法院或权威机构裁决
senses.example: The council remitted the planning case to a public inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把规划案提交公开调查。
senses.why: Cases travel in both directions, and this sense keeps the sending image but changes what is sent.
senses.whyCN: 案件可以在两边之间往返，这个义项保留「送出」的意象，只是换了被送的东西。

senses.title: The range of duties in British English
senses.definition: the area of responsibility or control of a group or official
senses.definitionCN: 某个团体或官员负责、管辖的范围
senses.example: Public transport is outside the remit of this committee.
senses.exampleCN: 公共交通不在这届委员会的职权范围内。
senses.why: What is sent to a body defines what that body must handle, so the noun names its scope of work.
senses.whyCN: 被「送交」给某机构的事情界定了该机构的处理范围，于是名词义就指它的职权。

intro.en: Remit comes from Latin remittere, to send back or relax, from re-, back, and mittere, to send.
intro.cn: remit 来自拉丁语 remittere（送回、放松），由 re-（回）与 mittere（送）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root mei, to go or change place, lies behind the sending verbs.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 mei（行走、变换位置）是这些「送」动词背后的来源。

items.en: Mittere means to send, and remittere means to send back or let go.
items.cn: mittere 意为送，remittere 意为送回或放松。

items.en: Remissa is the noun for a sending back or a release of debt.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 remissa 是「退回」或「免债」的名词。

items.en: Remettre carries the double sense of sending and letting go.
items.cn: 古法语 remettre 保留了「送」与「放松」的双重意义。

items.en: English remit first appears with religious and legal forgiveness.
items.cn: 英语 remit 最早出现在宗教与法律的宽恕语境中。

items.en: Modern English adds banking remittance and the British noun sense of duties.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加银行汇款义，以及英式名词「职责」义。

note.en: Remit shares its Latin verbs with submit and permit, and it sits close to payment and forgiveness words.
note.cn: remit 与 submit、permit 共享拉丁动词词根，同时靠近付款与宽恕类词。

entries.definition: to send in a document for consideration
entries.definitionCN: 提交；同取拉丁词根 mittere

entries.definition: to allow to happen
entries.definitionCN: 允许；同取拉丁词根 mittere

entries.definition: to send out light, sound, or gas
entries.definitionCN: 发出；同取拉丁词根 mittere

entries.definition: something treated as true in an argument
entries.definitionCN: 前提；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the act of remitting
entries.definitionCN: 汇款或宽免的行为（少用）

entries.definition: to move money from one account to another
entries.definitionCN: 转账

entries.definition: to stop blaming someone or cancel a debt
entries.definitionCN: 宽恕；免除

entries.definition: to become less strong
entries.definitionCN: 减弱；缓和

normalIntro.en: Remit is re- plus mit, the Latin sending root, so everything it names is sent back.
normalIntro.cn: remit 是 re- 加拉丁「送」词根 mit，它所指的一切都是「被打回去」的东西。

normal.en: Money is sent back home, so remit means to transfer money.
normal.cn: 钱被寄回家乡，所以 remit 表示汇款。

normal.en: A debt can also be sent away, which gives the sense of forgiveness.
normal.cn: 债务同样可以被「送走」，于是引申出免除宽恕。

normal.en: Same root as submit, permit, and emit, all about sending.
normal.cn: 与 submit、permit、emit 同根，都与「送」有关。

normal.en: The noun remittance names a sum of money sent abroad.
normal.cn: 名词 remittance 指汇往国外的款项。

normal.en: In British English, a remit is the scope of what a body may do.
normal.cn: 在英式英语中，remit 指某机构可以办的事项范围。

abstract.en: Imagine an envelope travelling back across the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一只信封越过大海被寄回去。

abstract.en: See a heavy ledger line being crossed out twice.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上一行账被重重划掉两道。

abstract.en: Watch a thermometer slide back down to normal.
abstract.cn: 想象体温计的水银柱滑回正常刻度。

examples.en: Volunteers remitted their extra funds to the small school.
examples.cn: 志愿者们把多余的资金汇给了那所小学校。

examples.en: The judge decided not to remit the remainder of the sentence.
examples.cn: 法官决定不免除剩余刑期。

examples.en: The question falls within the remit of the national authority.
examples.cn: 这个问题属于国家主管机构的职权范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞米特」——特快专递把钱瑞祥地寄到远方，再顺手把欠条撕掉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ mittere（送）→ remittere（送回、放松）→ 古法语 remettre → 英语 remit，核心义「把东西送回去」，钱送回即汇款，债送回即免除，病送回即消退。

sensesIntro.en: Remit begins with sending money back, then sending away a debt, then letting an illness retreat and a case be forwarded, and finally names the scope of work sent to a body.
sensesIntro.cn: remit 先说把钱寄回，继而说把债务送走，再说让病情退去、把案件转交，最后指交给某机构处理的事项范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an envelope sent back with the debt crossed out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被寄回的信封，里面的欠条被划掉。

branches.en: Sending money back home is the most common modern sense.
branches.cn: 把钱寄回家乡是现代最常见的义项。

branches.en: Sending a debt away produces the forgiveness sense.
branches.cn: 把债务送走产生了免除宽恕的义项。

branches.en: Symptoms and cases can both be sent back from the foreground.
branches.cn: 症状与案件都可以从前景中被退回去。

branches.en: Referring a matter defines who is responsible for it.
branches.cn: 移交一件事决定了谁对它负责。

branches.en: Both a remittance and a remission move something away from the sender.
branches.cn: 汇款与免债都是把某样东西从当事人那里移走。

intro.en: Remit is a Latin compound: the prefix re- joined to the verb mittere, with the noun remittance and the word remission sharing the same base.
intro.cn: remit 是拉丁语复合词：前缀 re- 加动词 mittere，名词 remittance 与 remission 共享同一词基。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means back or again, and mittere means to send or let go.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 re- 意为回、再，mittere 意为送、放开。

items.example: The prefix re- marks the backwards motion.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 标示向后运动。

items.example: Mittere supplies the idea of sending.
items.exampleCN: mittere 提供「送」的概念。

items.example: Remit keeps the two Latin senses.
items.exampleCN: remit 保留拉丁语的两层意义。

items.example: The bank remits funds abroad weekly.
items.exampleCN: 这家银行每周把资金汇往国外。

items.example: The fee was remitted by the court.
items.exampleCN: 费用已被法院免除。

items.example: The suffix -ance gives remittance.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 构成 remittance。

items.meaning: a sending or a letting go
items.example: The suffix -ssion gives remission.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ssion 构成 remission。

items.example: Submit uses sub- with the same root.
items.exampleCN: submit 用 sub- 与同一词根构词。

items.example: Permit uses per- with the same root.
items.exampleCN: permit 用 per- 与同一词根构词。

items.example: Emit uses e- with the same root.
items.exampleCN: emit 用 e- 与同一词根构词。

definition_zh: 残余；剩余部分；遗迹；零头布
definition_en: a small part or quantity that is left after the rest has gone or been used
core_image: 布匹裁完之后，桌上剩下的一小块碎布
scene: 布料裁好之后，桌角还剩下一小块碎布。After the cloth was cut, a small remnant of fabric was left on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 remnant 是「剩余部分」（第 1 个义项：用过或用掉之后剩下的部分）；句意：布料裁剪之后，桌上还剩一小块碎布。场景要点：裁剪台、剪刀、碎布边角。

pos.zh: 残余；剩余部分；遗迹；零头布

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，义为「剩下；仍然是」
同根名词，义为「剩余物；遗体；遗迹」
同根名词，义为「余数；剩余部分」

senses.title: A small part that is left
senses.definition: a small part or amount that remains after most of something has been used or removed
senses.definitionCN: 某物大部分已被用完或移走之后剩下的少量部分
senses.example: Only a remnant of the cake was left on the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 盘子里只剩下蛋糕的一小块。
senses.why: The base is the Latin verb that means to remain, so the noun names whatever is left behind.
senses.whyCN: 词基是拉丁语中表示「留下」的动词，所以这个名词专指留下来的那一点东西。

senses.title: Surviving trace of an earlier time
senses.definition: a part of something older that has survived when the rest has disappeared
senses.definitionCN: 其余部分已消失、而这一部分仍存留的旧日遗迹
senses.example: The wall is a remnant of an ancient fortress.
senses.exampleCN: 这段城墙是一座古堡垒的遗迹。
senses.why: When centuries remove most of a thing, what still stands is the remnant in the historical sense.
senses.whyCN: 当岁月把一样东西的大部分都抹掉，仍然立着的那部分就是历史意义上的遗迹。

senses.title: Leftover piece of cloth
senses.definition: a small piece of cloth left over from a larger piece that has been cut
senses.definitionCN: 从更大块布料上裁剪之后剩下的小块布
senses.example: She sewed the remnants into a quilt for the baby.
senses.exampleCN: 她把零头布缝成一床小被子给孩子。
senses.why: Tailors once used the word for cloth left on the table, and that workshop sense survives in modern sewing.
senses.whyCN: 裁缝曾用这个词指留在台面上的布，这一作坊义在现代缝纫中延续下来。

senses.title: A small surviving group
senses.definition: a small group of a people, species, or custom that has survived in great decline
senses.definitionCN: 在大量减少后仍存留下来的少量人群、物种或习俗
senses.example: Only a remnant of the original forest survives.
senses.exampleCN: 原始森林只残存下来一小片。
senses.why: The same leftover image applies to living things, where the small remainder is a threatened minority.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「剩下一点」的意象用于生物身上，那一点剩余就成了数量急剧减少的小群体。

intro.en: Remnant comes from Old French remenant, derived from the Latin verb remanere, to remain behind.
intro.cn: remnant 来自古法语 remenant，源出拉丁语动词 remanere（留下、滞留）。

items.en: Remanere means to stay behind or be left, built on manere, to stay.
items.cn: remanere 意为留在后面、被留下，由 manere（停留）构成。

items.en: Remanentia is used for what is left over.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 remanentia 表示剩余之物。

items.en: Remenant is both an adjective and a noun for what remains.
items.cn: 古法语 remenant 既是形容词也是名词，表示剩下的东西。

items.en: Remnant enters English with the sense of a leftover or trace.
items.cn: remnant 在十四世纪进入英语，义为残留物或痕迹。

items.en: Modern English adds the ecology sense of a surviving population.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加生态学中「残存种群」的义项。

note.en: Remnant belongs to the remain family and sits close to leftover, trace, and fragment words.
note.cn: remnant 属于 remain 词族，同时靠近 leftover、trace 与 fragment 一类词。

entries.definition: to stay or be left after others have gone
entries.definitionCN: 留下；剩下

entries.definition: what is left, or the body of a dead person
entries.definitionCN: 剩余物；遗体；遗迹

entries.definition: the part that is left over
entries.definitionCN: 余数；剩余部分

entries.definition: remaining after something else has passed
entries.definitionCN: 残留的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to send money or forgive a debt
entries.definitionCN: 汇款；免除；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: food or material not used and kept
entries.definitionCN: 剩余的食物或材料

entries.definition: a very small sign that something existed
entries.definitionCN: 痕迹；迹象

entries.definition: a small broken piece of something
entries.definitionCN: 碎片；片段

normalIntro.en: Remnant shares its Latin base with remain, so it always means the piece that stays behind.
normalIntro.cn: remnant 与 remain 共享拉丁词基，所以它总是指「留下来的那一部分」。

normal.en: Same family as remain, remains, and remainder, all about what is left.
normal.cn: 与 remain、remains、remainder 同族，都与「剩下」有关。

normal.en: A remnant of the past is a trace that survived when the rest vanished.
normal.cn: a remnant of the past 指其余部分消失后仍存留的遗迹。

normal.en: In sewing, remnants are the leftover pieces of cloth.
normal.cn: 在缝纫中，remnants 指剩下的零头布。

normal.en: Ecologists speak of a remnant population when a species shrinks.
normal.cn: 物种数量锐减时，生态学家会说 remnant population，即残存种群。

normal.en: Do not confuse remnant with remain, the verb form.
normal.cn: 不要把 remnant 与动词形式 remain 混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a scrap of bright cloth left on a cutting table.
abstract.cn: 想象裁剪台上留下一小片鲜亮的碎布。

abstract.en: See a single broken arch standing among fields.
abstract.cn: 想象田野间孤零零立着一段残破的拱门。

abstract.en: Imagine the last few grazing animals on a wide plain.
abstract.cn: 想象广阔平原上最后几只吃草的动物。

examples.en: A few remnants of the old wall can still be seen.
examples.cn: 还能看到老城墙的几处残迹。

examples.en: She kept the cloth remnants for a patchwork quilt.
examples.cn: 她把零头布留着拼成百衲被。

examples.en: The last remnants of the storm faded at sunset.
examples.cn: 暴风雨最后的余威在日落时消散了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞姆南特」——瑞气的布样只剩南边一小块，特小；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回、仍然）+ manere（停留）→ remanere（留下、滞留）→ medieval remanentia → 古法语 remenant → 英语 remnant，核心义「留下来的一点」。

sensesIntro.en: Remnant begins as the small piece left over, grows into the trace of an older time, narrows to leftover cloth, and finally names a small surviving group.
sensesIntro.cn: remnant 先指剩下的一小块，进而指旧时留下的遗迹，再专指零头布，最后指数量锐减后的残存群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scrap of cloth left on the cutting table.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁剪台上剩下的一小块碎布。

branches.en: The leftover piece is the basic and most general sense.
branches.cn: 剩下的一块是最基础、最泛用的义项。

branches.en: Extend the leftover in time and it becomes a historical trace.
branches.cn: 把「剩下」沿时间推进，它就变成历史遗迹。

branches.en: Narrow the field to cloth and the word names fabric offcuts.
branches.cn: 把范围收窄到布料，这个词就指零碎布头。

branches.en: Apply the leftover image to living things and it names a small surviving group.
branches.cn: 把「剩下」的意象用于生物，就指少量残存群体。

branches.en: Both an old ruin and a cloth scrap are the durable part of something larger that is gone.
branches.cn: 古老遗迹与零头布都是更大之物消失后仍耐存的部分。

intro.en: Remnant carries the Latin prefix re- and the verb base manere, and its English relatives include remain, remains, and remainder.
intro.cn: remnant 带着拉丁前缀 re- 与动词词基 manere，英语亲属词有 remain、remains 与 remainder。

latinIntro.en: Latin manere means to stay, and with re- it gives remanere, to remain behind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manere 意为停留，加上 re- 就得 remanere（留在后面）。

items.example: The prefix re- adds the idea of being left behind.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 加上「被留在后面」之意。

items.example: Manere is the staying base of the word.
items.exampleCN: manere 是这个词「停留」的词基。

items.example: Remanere gives the core leftover idea.
items.exampleCN: remanere 提供「剩下」的核心概念。

items.example: Remenant is the direct French source.
items.exampleCN: remenant 是直接的古法语来源。

items.example: Remnant keeps the concrete leftover sense.
items.exampleCN: remnant 保留具体的「剩余」含义。

items.example: The site holds remnants of old houses.
items.exampleCN: 遗址中保存着一些旧屋残迹。

items.example: Remain is the verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: remain 是该词族的动词。

items.example: Remainder is the formal leftover noun.
items.exampleCN: remainder 是正式的「剩余物」名词。

items.example: Remains is common for ruins and bodies.
items.exampleCN: remains 常用于遗迹与遗体。

items.example: Permanent shares the staying root in manere.
items.exampleCN: permanent 共享同一个表示停留的词根。

definition_zh: 报酬；酬劳；薪水；赔付
definition_en: the pay or reward that someone receives in return for work done or services given
core_image: 干完活后递到手上的一封报酬，与付出恰好相抵
scene: 面试接近尾声，对方谈到这个岗位的待遇，说薪水视经验而定。At the end of the interview, the manager explained that the remuneration for this post depends on experience.
sceneCN: 这里 remuneration 是「薪酬、酬劳」（第 1 个义项：因工作或服务而得到的报酬）；句意：面试快结束时，经理说明这个岗位的薪酬取决于经验。

derivatives.zh: remuneration 去 -ion 加 -ate 得到的动词，义为「酬劳；付报酬」
remunerate 加 -ive 构成，义为「报酬丰厚的；有利可图的」
remunerative 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「以有利可图的方式」

senses.title: Pay for work done
senses.definition: the money or other reward a person receives for work or services
senses.definitionCN: 人们因工作或服务而获得的金钱或其他回报
senses.example: Nurses often feel their remuneration does not match their responsibilities.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们常觉得自己的报酬与职责并不相称。
senses.why: Latin remunerare means to repay, so the core image is a gift handed back in return for a service.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 remunerare 意为「回报、偿付」，所以核心画面是为某项服务而回敬的一份酬答。

senses.title: An official pay scheme
senses.definition: the system or standards by which employees in an organisation are paid
senses.definitionCN: 组织给员工支付工资所依据的制度或标准
senses.example: The board adopted a new remuneration policy for senior staff.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会为高级职员通过了新的薪酬政策。
senses.why: Once pay is given regularly to many people, the single repayment becomes a rule that fixes how much each person gets.
senses.whyCN: 当报酬要按期发给许多人时，单次的「回敬」就变成了一套规定每人拿多少的规则。

senses.title: High pay as a reward for effort
senses.definition: generous pay that is seen as a fitting reward for hard or valuable work
senses.definitionCN: 被视为对辛苦或有价值工作的适当回报的优厚报酬
senses.example: The footballer accepted a large remuneration for the extra matches.
senses.exampleCN: 这名球员为了额外的比赛接受了丰厚的酬报。
senses.why: Because the Latin verb is about giving back in equal measure, the word can praise a reward that truly matches the effort.
senses.whyCN: 由于拉丁语动词讲的是等量地回给，这个词也可以用来称赞一份真与付出相称的回报。

senses.title: Compensation for a loss or wrong
senses.definition: money paid to make up for damage, loss, or unfair treatment
senses.definitionCN: 为弥补损害、损失或不公待遇而支付的金钱
senses.example: Tenants may claim remuneration for the months they could not use the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 租户可就无法使用公寓的那几个月申请补偿。
senses.why: Repaying a service and repaying a loss are the same gesture, so legal language borrows the word for compensation.
senses.whyCN: 偿付服务与弥补损失本是同一个动作，法律用语便把这个词借去表示赔偿。

senses.title: Spiritual reward
senses.definition: a reward of the spirit or the afterlife, especially in old religious writing
senses.definitionCN: 精神上或来世的回报，多见于古老的宗教文字
senses.example: Early sermons promised heavenly remuneration to those who gave to the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 早期布道许诺：施舍穷人者将得到天国的报偿。
senses.why: When pay is not money, the word stretches to any return that a good act earns, including in the next world.
senses.whyCN: 当「报酬」不是金钱时，这个词便扩展到善行所得的任何回报，包括来世的那一份。

intro.en: Remuneration is the English noun from Latin remunerari, to repay, and it keeps the image of a gift given back for a service.
intro.cn: remuneration 是源自拉丁语 remunerari（偿付、回报）的英语名词，保留着「为服务而回敬一份礼物」的意象。

items.en: The noun munus means a duty, a service, or a gift, and is also behind municipal and common.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 munus 意为职责、服务或礼物，也是 municipal 与 common 的词源。

items.en: Munus, dative muneri, pairs with re-, back, to give the verb remunerari, to repay or reward.
items.cn: munus（与格 muneri）与表示「回」的前缀 re- 结合，构成动词 remunerari，意为「偿付、报偿」。

items.en: The noun remuneratio, a repaying, is passed with the rest of the Latin vocabulary into European languages.
items.cn: 名词 remuneratio（偿付）随拉丁词汇一起被传递到欧洲各语言中。

items.en: Old French remuneration carries the noun towards English, where the earliest records appear in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 remuneration 把这个名词带向英语，英语最早的记录见于十四世纪晚期。

items.en: In Middle English the word often means reward or repayment of any kind, including a religious one.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个词常指任何形式的酬报或补偿，也包括宗教意义上的报偿。

items.en: Modern usage concentrates on pay and on compensation, and the older religious sense survives mainly in quotations.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在薪酬与赔偿上，古老的宗教义项主要保存在引文里。

note.en: Remuneration is the formal word for pay that has been earned, and it sits beside shorter words for salary, wages, and fees.
note.cn: remuneration 是表示「挣得的薪酬」的正式用词，与表示工资、酬金与费用的短词相邻。

entries.definition: to pay someone for work or a service
entries.definitionCN: 酬劳某人；给某人付报酬，是 remuneration 的动词形式

entries.definition: giving good payment or profit
entries.definitionCN: 报酬丰厚的；有利可图的

entries.definition: relating to a town or city and its government
entries.definitionCN: 市政的；地方政府的，与 remunerari 同出拉丁语 munus（职责）

entries.definition: fixed pay made regularly, usually monthly
entries.definitionCN: 薪水；薪金，指按月等固定周期发放的报酬

entries.definition: pay for work measured by hours or output
entries.definitionCN: 工资，常按小时或产量计酬，多用复数

entries.definition: money paid for loss, injury, or hardship
entries.definitionCN: 赔偿金；补偿，与第四个义项接近

normalIntro.en: Remuneration is built on Latin munus, a duty or gift, with re- meaning back, so it is a gift returned for work.
normalIntro.cn: remuneration 建立在拉丁语 munus（职责或礼物）之上，加上表示「回」的 re-，就是为工作而回敬的礼物。

normal.en: Re- plus mune plus -ration: something given back for a duty performed.
normal.cn: re- 加 mune 再加 -ration：为履行的职责而回给的东西。

normal.en: Common and municipal share the munus root, where munus means a shared duty.
normal.cn: common 与 municipal 共享 munus 词根，其中 munus 指共同的职责。

normal.en: The verb is remunerate, the adjective is remunerative, and the noun is remuneration.
normal.cn: 动词是 remunerate，形容词是 remunerative，名词是 remuneration。

normal.en: In business writing, remuneration is the neutral word for pay.
normal.cn: 在商务写作里，remuneration 是表示「薪酬」的中性词。

normal.en: A remuneration package means the whole bundle of pay, bonus, and benefits.
normal.cn: remuneration package 指薪水、奖金与福利合在一起的整体待遇。

abstract.en: Picture a craftsman handing over a finished table and receiving a folded note in return.
abstract.cn: 想象工匠交出一张做好的桌子，换回一张对折的纸币。

abstract.en: See a notice board on which every job title is followed by a number, the pay fixed by rule.
abstract.cn: 想象一块告示牌，每个职位名称后面都跟着一个数字，那是按规矩定下的薪酬。

abstract.en: Think of a hand that gives back more than it takes, because the work was heavy and well done.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手回给的比拿走的多，因为那份工作又重又做得好。

examples.en: The union is demanding better remuneration for night shifts.
examples.cn: 工会要求夜班获得更好的报酬。

examples.en: She accepted the post because the remuneration was fair.
examples.cn: 她接受了这个职位，因为报酬合理。

examples.en: Farm workers often receive part of their remuneration in food and lodging.
examples.cn: 农场工人往往有一部分报酬以食宿形式支付。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞缪纳瑞」谐音「锐木拿锐」，想象把锐利的木头连同锐利的手艺一起交出去，换回一份额外的回礼；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 remunerari（偿付、报偿）：前缀 re-（回、再）加 munus（职责；礼物）及其与格 muneri，字面为「以礼物回敬职责」；名词 remuneratio 加 -ation 后即「报酬」。

sensesIntro.en: Remuneration moves from a single repayment for work, to the rules that set pay, to generous reward, to compensation for loss, and finally to a spiritual return.
sensesIntro.cn: remuneration 从为一次工作付出的报酬，扩展到规定薪酬的制度、与付出相称的优厚回报、对损失的补偿，最后延伸到精神上的报偿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded payment handed back for work done.
core.cn: 核心意象：为已做的工作回递过去的一份报酬。

branches.en: The plain sense is money received for work.
branches.cn: 最基本的义项是因工作收到的钱。

branches.en: Repeated pay turns into a written rule.
branches.cn: 反复支付的报酬会固化成书面规则。

branches.en: A reward that matches effort is the generous side of the word.
branches.cn: 与付出相称的回报，是这个词偏向「丰厚」的一面。

branches.en: Compensation for loss keeps only the gesture of repaying.
branches.cn: 赔偿只保留了「回偿」这个动作本身。

branches.en: Religious writing extends the return beyond this world.
branches.cn: 宗教文字把这份回报延伸到了此世之外。

intro.en: Remuneration is a Latin noun of repayment, with the prefix re- and the root munus, and English builds remunerate and remunerative on it.
intro.cn: remuneration 是一个拉丁语「偿付」名词，由前缀 re- 与词根 munus 构成，英语又围绕它造出 remunerate 与 remunerative。

latinIntro.en: Latin munus means a duty or a gift, and remunerari means to repay, so the family always joins service with return.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 munus 意为职责或礼物，remunerari 意为偿付，因此这个词族始终把「职责」与「回给」连在一起。

items.example: Munus gives the word its idea of duty.
items.exampleCN: munus 给这个词带来「职责」的观念。

items.example: The dative muneri links the gift to the duty it answers.
items.exampleCN: 与格形式 muneri 把礼物与它所回应的职责连在一起。

items.example: Re- marks the giving back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 标记「回给」。

items.example: Remunerari is the source verb.
items.exampleCN: remunerari 是源头的动词。

items.example: Remuneratio adds the noun ending to the verb.
items.exampleCN: remuneratio 在动词后加上名词词尾。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The ending turns the action into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动作变成了一个可指称的事物。

items.example: Remunerate is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: remunerate 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms remunerative.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 remunerative。

items.example: Remunerative work pays well.
items.exampleCN: remunerative work 指报酬好的工作。

definition_zh: 演绎；表演版本；译文；（对条文等的）解释；引渡
definition_en: a particular performance, translation, or interpretation of a work, or the act of surrendering someone to another authority
core_image: 同一条旋律换一种乐器重新奏出，骨子里还是它
scene: 同一首老歌，爵士乐队只用贝斯和萨克斯重新演奏了一遍，味道完全不同。The jazz band played a slow rendition of the old song with only a bass and a saxophone.
sceneCN: 这里 rendition 是「演绎、演奏版本」（第 1 个义项：对乐曲或作品的某种具体表演）；句意：这支爵士乐队只用贝斯和萨克斯，缓慢地演绎了这首老歌。

pos.zh: 演绎；表演版本；译文；解释；引渡

collocations.zh: 这首诗的一种译文（或诵读版本）
忠实的译文；忠实的演绎
非常规引渡（绕过正常程序的移交）

derivatives.zh: rendition 去 -ition 后与 render 同源，义为「使成为；给予；翻译；演奏」
render 加 -ing 构成，义为「译文；演绎；渲染图」
render 加 -able 构成，义为「可表现的；可渲染的」

senses.title: A performed version of a piece
senses.definition: a particular way in which a song, role, or other work is performed
senses.definitionCN: 一首歌、一个角色或其他作品被表演出来的一种具体方式
senses.example: Her rendition of the anthem brought the crowd to its feet.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这首颂歌的演绎让全场起立。
senses.why: Latin reddere means to give back, and a performance gives the work back to an audience in the performer own way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 reddere 意为「交还」，而表演就是把作品以表演者自己的方式交还给听众。

senses.title: A translation or version of a text
senses.definition: a translation or version of a text into another language or form
senses.definitionCN: 把文本译成另一种语言或另一种形式的版本
senses.example: This prose rendition of the letter reads far more naturally.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信的这个散文译本读起来自然得多。
senses.why: Handing a text back in another language is another kind of return, so the word leaves the stage for the page.
senses.whyCN: 用另一种语言把文本交还出来也是一种回给，因此这个词从舞台走进了书页。

senses.title: An interpretation of a law or clause
senses.definition: the interpretation that an authority gives to a law, clause, or rule
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构对法律、条款或规则所作的解释
senses.example: The court rejected the minister rendition of the clause.
senses.exampleCN: 法院驳回了部长对该条款的解释。
senses.why: A rule is also something rendered, since an official voice gives it back in concrete terms for the people who must follow it.
senses.whyCN: 规则同样是被「交还」的东西，因为官方要用具体的说法把它交给必须遵守的人。

senses.title: Surrender of a person to another state
senses.definition: the act of handing a person over to the authorities of another country or legal system
senses.definitionCN: 把人移交给另一个国家或另一套法律体系的当局
senses.example: The case raised questions about the government rendition of suspects.
senses.exampleCN: 这起案件引发了人们对政府引渡嫌疑人的质疑。
senses.why: Reddere is to hand over, so the word keeps its older bite: a body returned to those who hold the power.
senses.whyCN: reddere 就是「交出」，所以这个词保留了更锋利的一层：把一个人交还给掌权者。

senses.title: A visual representation of data
senses.definition: a representation of data or a scene produced by a computer for viewing
senses.definitionCN: 计算机为观看而绘出的数据或场景呈现
senses.example: The software produces a detailed rendition of the building before it is built.
senses.exampleCN: 这款软件能在建筑落成前生成详细的建筑呈现图。
senses.why: Graphics software also gives data back as a picture, and the word follows it into computing.
senses.whyCN: 图形软件也是把数据以图像的形式交还出来，这个词便随之进入计算机领域。

intro.en: Rendition comes through French from Latin redditio, a giving back, built on red- plus dare, to give, and it is a close cousin of the verb render.
intro.cn: rendition 经法语来自拉丁语 redditio（交还），由 red- 与 dare（给）构成，与动词 render 是近亲。

items.en: Dare means to give, and it is also behind data, the things given.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，也是 data（被给出的东西）的词源。

items.en: Reddere joins red-, back, to dare and means to give back, hand over, or render.
items.cn: reddere 把表示「回」的 red- 加在 dare 前，意为交还、交出、呈现。

items.en: The abstract noun redditio, a giving back, is formed on the participle of reddere.
items.cn: 抽象名词 redditio（交还）由 reddere 的分词形式加名词词尾构成。

items.en: French rendition brings the noun into English, where it is first recorded in the late sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 rendition 把这个名词带入英语，英语最早记录见于十六世纪晚期。

items.en: The first English senses are about giving up a place or a person, and about rendering a text.
items.cn: 英语最早的意义涉及让出地点或交出人物，以及把文本呈现出来。

items.en: In modern English the word concentrates on performances and translations, while the surrender sense survives in law and journalism.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词集中在表演与翻译上，而「移交」义只保留在法律与新闻语境里。

note.en: Rendition is the noun of giving something back, near render and rendering in form and near performance and translation in meaning.
note.cn: rendition 是表示「交还、呈现」的名词，形式上亲于 render 与 rendering，意义上亲于表演与翻译。

entries.definition: to cause to become, give, translate, or perform
entries.definitionCN: 使成为；给予；翻译；演奏，与 rendition 同出拉丁语 reddere

entries.definition: a translation, a performance, or a computed image
entries.definitionCN: 译文；演绎；渲染图，由 render 加 -ing 构成

entries.definition: the act of giving up or handing something over
entries.definitionCN: 交出；投降，与 rendition 同出拉丁语 reddere

entries.definition: able to be rendered
entries.definitionCN: 可表现的；可渲染的

entries.definition: the act of presenting a play, concert, or other entertainment
entries.definitionCN: 演出；表演，是最常见的一般说法

entries.definition: a particular form of something that differs from other forms
entries.definitionCN: 版本；说法，强调与其他形式不同

entries.definition: an explanation of the meaning of something
entries.definitionCN: 解释；诠释，与第三个义项接近

normalIntro.en: Rendition shares the Latin source reddere with render, and the -ition ending marks it as the noun of a giving back.
normalIntro.cn: rendition 与 render 同出拉丁语 reddere，而 -ition 词尾标明它是「交还」的名词。

normal.en: The da- root means to give, and rend- means giving back.
normal.cn: da- 词根意为「给」，rend- 则由「回」加「给」构成。

normal.en: Render is the verb and rendering is the everyday noun, so rendition is the formal doublet.
normal.cn: 动词是 render，日常名词是 rendering，rendition 则是更正式的同源异形词。

normal.en: Give a rendition of a song is the standard concert phrase.
normal.cn: 「give a rendition of a song」是音乐会上标准的说法。

normal.en: An extraordinary rendition is a handover of a suspect outside the usual legal route.
normal.cn: 「extraordinary rendition」指不走常规法律途径的移交。

normal.en: Translators speak of a faithful rendition of a poem.
normal.cn: 译者会说一首诗的「a faithful rendition」，即忠实译文。

abstract.en: Picture the same melody played first on a piano and then on a guitar, one tune in two bodies.
abstract.cn: 想象同一首旋律先用钢琴、再用吉他奏出，一个曲调换了两个身体。

abstract.en: See a thick book in one language closed and an identical book in another language opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书在一种语言里合上，又在另一种语言里打开一本内容相同的书。

abstract.en: Think of a key passed from one hand to another, never dropped and never changed.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙从一只手交到另一只手，既没掉下，也没被换掉。

examples.en: The choir gave a beautiful rendition of the old hymn.
examples.cn: 合唱团优美地演绎了这首古老的赞美诗。

examples.en: His rendition of the poem loses the rhyme of the original.
examples.cn: 他对这首诗的译文失去了原作的韵脚。

examples.en: Critics praised her rendition of the difficult soprano role.
examples.cn: 评论家称赞了她对这个高难女高音角色的演绎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「润迪申」谐音「认底身」：把一首歌认认真真从头到尾演一遍，底子还是那首歌；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 reddere（交还、交出）：red-（回）加 dare（给），名词 redditio 意为「交还」；经法语 rendition 进入英语，核心义「把作品或人交还出来」。

sensesIntro.en: Rendition starts from the act of giving something back as a performance, then as a translation, an interpretation, a surrender, and finally a computed image.
sensesIntro.cn: rendition 从「把作品以表演交还」出发，再延伸到译文、对条文的解释、人的移交，最后到计算机生成的图像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same tune coming back in a different body.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个曲调换了一个身体重新出现。

branches.en: Performance is the most common sense today.
branches.cn: 表演是今天最常见的义项。

branches.en: A translation is the give-back that crosses a language.
branches.cn: 译文是跨过语言的交还。

branches.en: Interpreting a rule is a give-back into plain words.
branches.cn: 解释规则是把条文交还成明白的话。

branches.en: Handing over a person keeps the oldest legal meaning.
branches.cn: 移交人保留了最古老的法律义。

branches.en: A computer image is a give-back of data.
branches.cn: 计算机图像是把数据交还出来。

intro.en: Rendition is a Latin action noun built on red- and dare, and the same stem runs through render, rendering, and surrender.
intro.cn: rendition 是由 red- 与 dare 构成的拉丁语动作名词，同一词干贯穿 render、rendering 与 surrender。

latinIntro.en: Latin dare means to give, and red- adds the idea of returning, so the family always means to give back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dare 意为给，red- 添加「回来」之意，所以这个词族始终表示「交还」。

items.example: Red- marks the returning of what is given.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 red- 标记所给之物的回返。

items.example: The da- root also appears in data.
items.exampleCN: da- 词根也出现在 data 中。

items.example: Reddere is the source verb of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: reddere 是整个词族的源头动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The ending makes an action noun out of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变为动作名词。

items.meaning: to cause, give, translate, or perform
items.example: Render is the short verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: render 是这个词族里简短的动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或产物的词尾
items.example: The ending forms rendering.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 rendering。

items.example: The ending forms renderable.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 renderable。

items.example: The prefix builds surrender on the same base.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在同源词根上构成 surrender。

items.meaning: to give up or hand over
items.example: Surrender means to give over completely.
items.exampleCN: surrender 意为完全交出。

definition_zh: 更新；恢复；续订；重续；（城市、精神等的）复兴
definition_en: the act of making something new or valid again, or the process of a place or a spirit coming back to life
core_image: 枯枝上重新冒出的一层新绿
scene: 旧城区改造之后，废弃的码头变成了公园，街角又开满小店。After the urban renewal, the old docks became a park and shops reopened on every corner.
sceneCN: 这里 renewal 是「更新改造、复兴」（第 4 个义项：城市或地区重新焕发生机）；句意：城市更新之后，旧码头变成了一座公园，街角又重开了店铺。

derivatives.zh: renewal 的动词形式，义为「更新；续订」
renew 加 -able 构成，义为「可再生的；可续期的」
renew 加 -ed 构成，义为「重新焕发的；重新的」

senses.title: The act of making something fresh again
senses.definition: the act of making something old, worn, or used seem new again
senses.definitionCN: 使陈旧、磨损或用过的东西重新变新的行为
senses.example: The library closed for a year for a full renewal of its reading rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆闭馆一年，对阅览室进行整体翻新。
senses.why: The word is re- plus new, so the core image is an old thing putting out fresh growth, and the plainest sense is making it new again.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 re- 加 new，核心画面是旧物重新长出新芽，最直白的义项就是「让它再新一次」。

senses.title: A new freshness of mind or spirit
senses.definition: a return of energy, hope, or faith after a low or tired period
senses.definitionCN: 在低落或疲惫之后重新获得精力、希望或信心
senses.example: A week by the sea brought a quiet renewal of spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 海边的一周让精神悄然复苏。
senses.why: A tired body or spirit can be made new, so renewal runs inward and becomes a sense of being refreshed.
senses.whyCN: 疲惫的身体或精神同样可以「变新」，于是 renewal 转向内心，成为一种重新振作的感觉。

senses.title: Extending something that expires
senses.definition: the act of arranging for a contract, membership, or document to stay valid for longer
senses.definitionCN: 安排合同、会籍或证件继续有效的行为
senses.example: The lease requires a renewal every three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这份租约每三年需要续签一次。
senses.why: Making a thing new in time is the administrative version of the same movement, since the old date is pushed back and freshness is granted on paper.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上让某物变新，是同一个动作的行政版本：旧日期被往后推，新意在纸面上重新被授予。

senses.title: Revival of a place or an institution
senses.definition: the process by which a city area, an institution, or a movement comes back to life
senses.definitionCN: 城区、机构或运动重新焕发生机的过程
senses.example: The harbour renewal brought jobs and visitors back to the town.
senses.exampleCN: 港口复兴让小镇重新有了工作和游客。
senses.why: A whole district can grow new again in the way a branch does in spring, which stretches the word to large public revival.
senses.whyCN: 整个街区也能像春天枝条一样重新长出新生，这个词便扩展到大型的公共复兴。

senses.title: Beginning again after a break
senses.definition: the act of starting an activity or a relationship again after it has stopped
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动或关系停止之后重新开始的行为
senses.example: The renewal of peace talks surprised many observers.
senses.exampleCN: 和谈重新启动让许多观察人士感到意外。
senses.why: Anything that stops can start afresh, so the word also names the restart of a practice or a friendship.
senses.whyCN: 凡停下来的一切都可以重新开始，于是这个词也用来指某项做法或某段友情的重启。

senses.title: Periodic fresh energy from a source
senses.titleCN: 可再生能源的不断补充
senses.definition: the natural or repeated replacement of a resource, as in renewable energy
senses.definitionCN: 资源被自然或反复补足，如可再生能源中所说
senses.example: The town now runs largely on energy from constant renewal of wind and sun.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇现在的用电，大多来自风和阳光源源不断的补充。
senses.why: When nature keeps replacing what is used, the word hardens into a technical term about energy.
senses.whyCN: 当自然不断补足被用掉的部分时，这个词便固定为有关能源的术语。

intro.en: Renewal is the English noun formed from renew, itself re- plus the native adjective new, with the noun ending -al.
intro.cn: renewal 是由 renew 加名词词尾 -al 构成的英语名词，而 renew 本身又是前缀 re- 加本土形容词 new。

items.en: The adjective niwe means new and later becomes modern English new.
items.cn: 古英语形容词 niwe 意为「新的」，后来演变为现代英语的 new。

items.en: The prefix re-, inherited from Latin, means again or back.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 源自拉丁语，意为「再次」或「回」。

items.en: The parallel French verb renouveler and its noun renouvellement may have supported the English forms.
items.cn: 法语中平行的动词 renouveler 及其名词 renouvellement 可能对英语形式起了推动作用。

items.en: The verb renew appears first in the late fourteenth century, and the noun renewal follows in the following century.
items.cn: 动词 renew 最早出现在十四世纪晚期，名词 renewal 在下一个世纪随之出现。

items.en: The noun extends to the extending of contracts and to the spiritual reawakening prized in religious writing.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到合同的续期，以及在宗教文字中备受珍视的精神觉醒。

items.en: Urban renewal and renewable energy give the word its two best known modern settings.
items.cn: 「urban renewal」与「renewable energy」为这个词提供了两个最著名的现代语境。

note.en: Renewal is the noun of making new again, next to renew and renewable in form and next to restoration and revival in meaning.
note.cn: renewal 是「使重新变新」的名词，形式上与 renew、renewable 相邻，意义上与恢复、复兴相邻。

entries.definition: to begin something again or make it valid once more
entries.definitionCN: 重新开始；使重新有效，是 renewal 的动词形式

entries.definition: able to be replaced by nature or extended in time
entries.definitionCN: 可再生的；可续期的

entries.definition: having become fresh or strong again
entries.definitionCN: 重新焕发的；重新的

entries.definition: recently made or not existing before
entries.definitionCN: 新的，是 renewal 的本土词根

entries.definition: the act of returning something to an earlier good condition
entries.definitionCN: 修复；恢复，强调回到原状

entries.definition: a return to life, popularity, or use after a decline
entries.definitionCN: 复兴；复苏，与第四个义项接近

entries.definition: the act of making something last longer or cover more
entries.definitionCN: 延长；延期，与第三个义项接近

normalIntro.en: Renewal is re- plus new plus -al, a prefix, a native word, and a noun ending laid one on another.
normalIntro.cn: renewal 由 re-、new 与 -al 层层相加而成：一个前缀、一个本土词、一个名词词尾。

normal.en: Re- plus new makes renew, and -al turns it into renewal.
normal.cn: re- 加 new 得到 renew，再加 -al 变成 renewal。

normal.en: Renewal and renewable come from the same stem, but one is a thing and one is a quality.
normal.cn: renewal 与 renewable 同源，但一个是事物，一个是性质。

normal.en: Urban renewal is the standard phrase for remaking old city districts.
normal.cn: 「urban renewal」是改造旧城区的标准说法。

normal.en: Contract renewal, lease renewal, and passport renewal all mean pushing a date forward.
normal.cn: 「contract renewal」「lease renewal」与「passport renewal」都指把日期往后推。

normal.en: The noun often follows an article: a renewal of hope, a renewal of the lease.
normal.cn: 这个名词常跟在冠词后：「a renewal of hope」「a renewal of the lease」。

abstract.en: Picture bare branches in late winter and then the first green tips pushing out.
abstract.cn: 想象冬末光秃的枝条，随后第一批绿尖冒出来。

abstract.en: See a yellowed passport page being stamped again with a fresh date.
abstract.cn: 想象泛黄的护照页上又被盖上一个新的日期。

abstract.en: Think of an empty factory hall whose windows are lit again by small shops.
abstract.cn: 想象一座空荡的厂房大厅，窗户又被一家家小店点亮。

examples.en: The renewal of the magazine subscription cost less than expected.
examples.cn: 这份杂志续订的费用比预想的低。

examples.en: Urban renewal has changed the face of the district.
examples.cn: 城市更新改变了这个地区的面貌。

examples.en: Spring brings a renewal of growth to the whole garden.
examples.cn: 春天让整座花园重新长出新的生机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞纽尔」谐音「瑞牛儿」：想象瑞丽的牛儿经过一冬，春天又长出一身新毛；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 re-（再次）加词根 new（新的），再加名词词尾 -al，字面即「使重新变新」这件事。

sensesIntro.en: Renewal keeps one idea, making new again, and applies it to objects, to the spirit, to deadlines, to whole districts, to fresh starts, and to natural energy.
sensesIntro.cn: renewal 始终守着「使重新变新」这一个观念，分别施加于物品、精神、期限、整片城区、重新开始以及自然能源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fresh green shoots on a bare branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：枯枝上重新冒出的新绿。

branches.en: Renewal of a thing is the plain physical sense.
branches.cn: 对物品的更新是最直白的物质义项。

branches.en: Renewal of spirit is the inward sense.
branches.cn: 精神复苏是向内的一面。

branches.en: Renewal of a document is the administrative sense.
branches.cn: 文书续期是行政层面的义项。

branches.en: Renewal of a city is the large public sense.
branches.cn: 城市更新是大型公共层面的义项。

branches.en: Both start something once more, as a talk restarts or as nature refills a supply.
branches.cn: 两者都让某物再一次开始：和谈重启，或自然补足供给。

intro.en: Renewal is one of the clearest prefix-plus-word formations in English, with a Latin prefix on a native base and an English noun ending.
intro.cn: renewal 是英语中最清晰的「前缀加单词」构词之一：拉丁前缀加在本土词根上，再加英语名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means again, and new is the native adjective for something recently made, so renewal is freshness granted a second time.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「再次」，new 是表示「新近形成」的本土形容词，因此 renewal 就是第二次授予的新意。

items.example: Re- repeats the making of something new.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示把「变新」再做一次。

items.example: Niwe is the Old English form of new.
items.exampleCN: niwe 是 new 的古英语形式。

items.example: New is the native base of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: new 是整个词的本土基础。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The ending turns renew into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 renew 变成名词。

items.meaning: to make new or valid again
items.example: Renew is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: renew 是这个名词背后的动词。

items.example: The ending forms renewable.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 renewable。

items.example: The ending forms renewed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 renewed。

items.example: The French noun is a parallel formation.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词是平行的构词。

definition_zh: 著名的；闻名的；享有盛誉的
definition_en: famous and admired for a particular skill, quality or achievement
core_image: 四周钟声响遍全城，人人都在念着一个名字
scene: 大学图书馆的墙上挂满旧照片，来访者总会谈起那位白发学者。The small town has long been renowned for its university and its quiet streets.
sceneCN: 这里 renowned 是「以……闻名」（第 1 个义项：因某种特长或事物而广受赞誉）；句意：这座小镇一直因它的大学和安静的街道而闻名。图中可辨识物件：图书馆、旧照片、钟楼。

pos.zh: 著名的；闻名的；享有盛誉的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词还原的名词，义为「声誉；名望」
形容词加 -ness 构成的抽象名词，义为「著名；盛名」
re- 换成 un- 的反向联想词，义为「无名的」，词源不同，只作对照

senses.title: Famous for a particular quality
senses.titleCN: 以某种特长或事物闻名
senses.definition: widely known and respected for a special skill, quality or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因为某种特长、品质或成就而广为人知、受到赞许
senses.example: The island is renowned for its clear water and coral reefs.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛以其清澈的海水和珊瑚礁而闻名。
senses.why: Re- is intensive here and noun meant to name, so renown is a name carried far and wide; renowned describes the person or place that name belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 re- 起加强作用，noun 意为「称呼、命名」，renown 就是被传得很远的名声；renowned 则形容拥有这份名声的人或地方。

senses.title: Highly admired, of high standing
senses.definition: held in high regard, especially in a profession or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 在某个行业或机构中受到高度敬重
senses.example: She became one of the most renowned doctors in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 她成为该地区最富盛名的医生之一。
senses.why: A name that travels far becomes a mark of standing, so renowned turns from mere fame into the respect a reputation earns.
senses.whyCN: 能传得很远的名声会自然变成地位标志，所以 renowned 从单纯的「出名」扩展为「因声誉而受尊敬」。

senses.title: Well-known in a wide circle
senses.definition: known to a very wide circle of people, often through public success
senses.definitionCN: 被很广的人群所知晓，常因公众层面的成功
senses.example: The festival has become renowned across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日已在全国广为人知。
senses.why: The re- intensity means the naming reaches every quarter, so the word also covers wide public knowledge without any special admiration.
senses.whyCN: 加强语气的 re- 表示「名声传遍各方」，所以这个词也用来指广为人知，而不必带有特别的崇敬。

intro.en: Renowned is the past participle of the now rare verb renown, from Old French renon, a name or fame.
intro.cn: renowned 来自如今少见的动词 renown 的过去分词，而 renown 出自古法语 renon（名字、名声）。

items.en: Renominare, meaning to name again, combined re- with nominare, to name.
items.cn: 拉丁语 renominare 意为「再次命名」，由 re-（再）加 nominare（命名）构成。

items.en: A popular form renonare is generally taken as the link between the Latin verb and the French noun.
items.cn: 一般认为通俗拉丁语形式 renonare 是拉丁语动词与法语名词之间的过渡环节。

items.en: Old French renon means a name or fame, and its participle renowné described a person with a great name.
items.cn: 古法语 renon 意为名字、名声，其分词 renowné 形容名声很大的人。

items.en: English borrowed renown as a noun in the fourteenth century and formed the adjective renowned from it.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入名词 renown，又由它造出形容词 renowned。

items.en: By the sixteenth century renowned is common in the fixed pattern be renowned for, naming the source of fame.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，renowned 已常见于固定说法 be renowned for 中，用它点出名声的来源。

items.en: Modern English keeps renown as a literary noun and uses renowned mainly as an adjective before a person or a place.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词 renown 作书面语，而 renowned 主要作形容词，放在人或地方之前。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same re- plus naming root; the near-meaning group gathers words of fame with different scope and tone.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「re- 加命名词根」的一族词；近义组收表示「出名」的词，适用范围和语气各不相同。

entries.definition: fame, especially for a special ability
entries.definitionCN: 名声；声望

entries.definition: to name someone for an office or an honour
entries.definitionCN: 提名；任命

entries.definition: important or worth noticing
entries.definitionCN: 显著的；值得注意的

entries.definition: known about by very many people
entries.definitionCN: 著名的；出名的

entries.definition: widely praised, often for a public achievement
entries.definitionCN: 著名的；久负盛名的

entries.definition: highly respected in a profession or a field
entries.definitionCN: 杰出的；享有盛名的

normalIntro.en: Renowned is the adjective of the noun renown, sitting on the re- plus noun root of naming.
normalIntro.cn: renowned 是名词 renown 的形容词，词根是 re- 再加上表示「命名」的 noun。

normal.en: Be renowned for names the reason for the fame, as in renowned for its wine.
normal.cn: be renowned for 点出名声的来源，例如 renowned for its wine 表示「以葡萄酒闻名」。

normal.en: Put renowned before the person or the place: a renowned expert, a renowned city.
normal.cn: renowned 放在人或地方之前：a renowned expert 指知名专家，a renowned city 指著名城市。

normal.en: Renowned is stronger than famous; it always carries respect.
normal.cn: renowned 比 famous 分量更重，总带有敬意。

normal.en: Renown keeps the noun meaning fame and appears as a formal word in writing.
normal.cn: renown 保留名词含义「名声」，是书面语中的正式用词。

normal.en: Notable and notable people share the naming root noun, so names connect to renown.
normal.cn: notable 与 notable people 共享同一个「命名」词根 noun，所以「名字」与「名声」相连。

abstract.en: Picture a bell tower ringing, and everybody in the town repeating one name.
abstract.cn: 想象钟楼响起，城里每个人都在重复同一个名字。

abstract.en: Imagine a scientist whose face is printed in every textbook, so the name sticks to the work.
abstract.cn: 想象一位科学家的面孔印在每本课本上，名字和工作紧紧相连。

abstract.en: Think of a village map with flags on it, every flag marking news of one person.
abstract.cn: 想象一张插满小旗的村庄地图，每面旗都标记着某人的消息。

examples.en: The region is renowned for its handmade ceramics.
examples.cn: 这一地区以手工陶瓷闻名。

examples.en: She is a renowned researcher in marine biology.
examples.cn: 她是海洋生物学领域一位声名卓著的研究者。

examples.en: The restaurant has become renowned far beyond the city walls.
examples.cn: 这家餐馆的名气早已传到了城墙之外远得多的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞闹恩的」——名声太响，满城「闹」得人尽皆知，自然就是知名的；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再、反复）+ nominare（命名）→ renominare「再次命名」→ 通俗拉丁语 renonare → 古法语 renon「名字、名声」→ 英语名词 renown → 形容词 renowned，核心义「名字被反复传扬」。
